traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Encelia farinosa: grows 1 m to 1.6 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Encelia farinosa: leaves 3 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Encelia farinosa: leaves 2 cm to 5 cm wide.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Encelia farinosa (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.63 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.63, branches 0.6. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a rounded shrub 0.6 to 1.2 m tall of silvery, felted, oval leaves crowded at the stem tips, covered in spring by yellow daisy heads held above the foliage on long stalks. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 0.8 m at 5 years and 1 m at 15. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: silver-white leaves, bright yellow heads.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Encelia farinosa (p. 123): woody below, much branched, a rounded bush; 'semi' for woody only in its lower part (woody would also fit).

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): blades ovate to lanceolate, wedge-shaped at the base, 3-nerved.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): slender petioles 1-4 cm long.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): simple blades.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): blades entire.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): entire, often wavy, rarely shallowly toothed (repand-dentate).

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): several heads in cymes or panicles on nearly naked branches, nodding in fruit.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): about 8-18 rays.

traits.phyllary_series.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): involucre in 3-4 graduated series.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): involucre 3.5-7 mm high; whole heads 1.8-4 cm wide across the rays.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): rays about 8-18.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): rays 7-15 mm long.

traits.ray_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): rays yellow. Word: yellow.

traits.disc_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): disc yellow; var. phenicodonta, in the south of the range, has disc florets purple above. Word: yellow.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): achenes about 4 mm long.

traits.pappus.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): pappus wanting.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, E. farinosa (p. 123): March to June.
